## Overview
[Saga invention] The sworn wolf-brotherhood (*Brolija*; each pack a *gauja* of five to nine), which calls itself *Dievo šunys*, "God's dogs". Folk sources: Baltic werewolf belief and the 1692 Thiess trial. The packs hold the [Iron Wolf's skull](../artifacts/wolf_skull.qmd) (since 1323) and give [Kęstutis](../characters/kestutis.qmd) the [silver wolf](../artifacts/silver_wolf.qmd) in 1345. About 120 in 1382; about 40 after the Vilnius massacre (Book I ch. 7) and the schism; 14 at Kūčios 1430 (V ch. 7); a dozen at Pabaiskas, 1 Sep 1435; Pilkoji lies down with the skull on 2 Nov 1449 (V ch. 28). The Flame-Keeper, burned at Palanga in March 1450, is the last (V ch. 29).

| I | Obey the flame; hold the doors in 1382 | Vilnius packs; Jonas rescues Vytautas (I ch. 25) | Shedding kin blood |
| II | Follow the flame, not the man | Hunters of the Unbound (II ch. 14); Kalvis at the lodge | Crossing the Dnieper, where the gift fails (II ch. 26) |

| IV | Survive the Church | Pilkoji becomes Vilkų Motina (IV ch. 6) | The flame going out |

## Patron Force
[Saga] [Šaknų Motina](../forces/root_mother.qmd), who made their bodies. They serve two masters (D10): the Root-Mother, and whoever keeps a Gediminid flame. Rule 2 forbids shedding Gediminid blood, and rule 9 says the pack answers the flame, not the man.

## Internal tensions
The 1382 schism split Vilnius packs (loyal to Jogaila's flame) from Kęstutis's nine. The order of the dead after 1430 is a ledger: four taken at Pabaiskas (V ch. 13), five that winter (V ch. 16), then Dobilas, Uosis and Pilkoji. The Order puts a bounty on their hides; the Church hunts them.

## Notable members
[Jonas](../characters/jonas.qmd), [The Flame-Keeper (Žiežirba)](../characters/flame_keeper.qmd); Pilkoji, Kalvis, Šešiapirštis, Kirmėlė and Spyglys have no wiki pages.
